checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: Recognizable F-35 configuration: one rear exhaust, two canted tails, no canards
must.why: The jet is a two-seat, F-15/F-14-style fighter with a long canopy and a boxy twin-engine rear. Its tails are nearly upright. It is not an F-35, which has a single seat.

must.item: Takeoff shows forward runway roll and lift-off
must.why: Frames 1-4 show the jet rolling down the runway and lifting off with the gear still down, moving forward.

must.item: Same aircraft design consistent between runway and airborne views
must.why: The runway jet and the airborne jet differ in canopy, intake and fuselage. The assistant's own message also said the jet might not match between shots.

must.item: All three labels appear exactly and are legible
must.why: The frames I was given cover only the two flight clips. The title cards are not among them, so the label text can't be checked.

must.item: Audible English narration on one engine and conventional takeoff, no F-35B hover claims
must.why: I can't hear the audio. The track is 10 s long and has sound, but its content is unknown. The planned script is correct in wording.

exact_text.read_as: Not visible in the frames provided; the title cards were not included.
Not visible in the frames provided.
Not visible in the frames provided.

faults.what: The aircraft is not a real F-35A. It is a two-seat fighter resembling an F-15 or F-14 hybrid, with a twin-engine look, so it breaks the 'real proportions' request.
The jet changes between the runway shot and the flying shot. The canopy, intakes, fuselage and framing all differ.
The labels sit on separate black cards, not over the footage. The user approved this method.
The narration was cut to fragments to fit the 2-second cards. The audio is 10 s against the stated 8.1 s video, so the sound may be out of sync.
The flight shot is a tight close-up. The jet is cut off at the frame edge and flies very low.

summary: The footage is photoreal and shows a real runway takeoff and a flight, but the jet is a two-seat F-15-style fighter, not an F-35A, and it changes between shots. The labels and narration could not be verified.
